data.content_ref: inline:Recovery synchronization is weak and in many cases wrong as distinguishing evidence. Simultaneous independent transient failures (e.g., a brief network partition or power glitch) can clear at nearly the same time across independent services, producing synchronized recovery without any shared cause; the target's own countercondition acknowledges this. Conversely, a shared cause with heterogeneous local recovery paths (different restart procedures, caches warming at different rates, operator response delays) can produce staggered recoveries that would be mistaken for independence under this criterion. The proposed narrow 10ms window is therefore neither necessary nor sufficient for identifying shared causation, so it does not reliably distinguish truly independent from apparently uncorrelated failures.
